findings.title: Under V2, deleting a client leaves its authz resource and permissions behind.
findings.body:
The new `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` guard means that when only `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is on, `ClientRemovedEvent` (and role and group removal events) do nothing. That stops the crash from `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`. But this PR adds per-client resources, named after the client id, in the admin-permissions resource server, and nothing removes them now.

Trigger: create a per-client permission on a client, then delete the client. The resource and its scope permission are left in the resource server. They still show up in `getClientsWithPermission` (through `findByType`), which returns ids of clients that no longer exist, and they pile up in the admin-permissions client.

Fix: add a V2 branch that removes the client's resource, or takes it out of its permissions, when the client is deleted, instead of skipping the event. I could not see whether another listener does this cleanup.

findings.title: V2 client permissions throw UnsupportedOperationException from methods that runtime callers still use.
findings.body:
Before this change, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returned the V1 `ClientPermissions`, which implements `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions` and similar methods. It now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, and those methods throw `UnsupportedOperationException`.

Callers that go through `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients()` can still reach them while ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on. Two examples:
- Legacy token exchange checks `canExchangeTo(...)` when exchanging to another client.
- The client admin endpoint `GET /clients/{id}/management/permissions` calls `isPermissionsEnabled(client)`.

With V2 enabled, these requests now fail with a 500 error. Before, they either worked or returned a proper answer.

I could not see whether those callers are gated off when V2 is enabled. If they are not, return a safe value instead of throwing: `false` from `canExchangeTo` and `isPermissionsEnabled`, and an empty map from `getPermissions`. Another option is to reject these calls with a 4xx error at the endpoint.

findings.title: Javadoc for void requireView() says it returns true.
findings.body: `requireView()` returns `void` and throws when access is denied, but its new Javadoc says it "Returns `true` if `canView()` returns `true`". The other `require*` methods in this interface say "Throws ForbiddenException if ...". Change this comment to match them.

findings.title: Javadoc for void requireViewClientScopes() says it returns true.
findings.body: `requireViewClientScopes()` is `void` and throws when access is denied, but its Javadoc says it "Returns `true` if `canViewClientScopes()` returns `true`". This contradicts the method signature and the wording of the other `require*` docs.

held.title: No null check on the all-clients resource before it is used.
held.body:
When no resource exists for the client, the code falls back to `getResourceTypeResource(...)` for the Clients type. It then passes the result to `findByResource` and calls `resource.getScopes()` without checking for null.

The Clients type is new in this change. If the resource-type resource does not exist yet for a realm's admin-permissions client, for example one set up before this change, every `canView`/`canManage` check that reaches this fallback fails with an NPE.

Fix: return `false` when `resource` is null after the fallback.
